newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA MONTHLY INFLATION SOARS TO 13.7 PCT IN JAN.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA MONTHLY INFLATION SOARS TO 13.7 PCT IN JAN.

text.p: Romania's monthly inflation soared to 13.7 percent in January from 10.3 percent last December, the National Statistics Board said on Wednesday.
The rise was triggered by an increase in fuel prices, which doubled in the New Year.
Year-on-year inflation leaped to 76.3 percent in January from 56.9 percent in December. The December figure was nearly triple the 20 percent target agreed with the International Monetary Fund.
Inflation is forecast to climb to a year-on-year 97 percent this year, with the government estimating a 41 percent level for the first quarter, following electricity, fuel and food price rises.
But it is expected to slow down towards the end of the year. The coaltion government, which replaced ex-communists last November, aims by December to reduce the monthly rate to about 2.2 percent.

The government this week announced a package of austerity measures to enable Romania to secure fresh credits totalling about $1.0 billion from international lenders to underpin reforms and put the economy on track.
